claims.statement: web/WEB-INF/web.xml declares exactly two filters, both mapped to /*: the Struts2 dispatcher (org.apache.struts2.dispatcher.filter.StrutsPrepareAndExecuteFilter with init-param contextConfigLocation=classpath:struts.xml) first, and Spring's CharacterEncodingFilter (encoding=UTF-8) second, plus a context-param and ContextLoaderListener for classpath:applicationContext.xml. It declares no servlet, welcome file, session config, security constraint or third filter.

Because the Struts filter is declared before the encoding filter it is the outer filter of the two, so UTF-8 is pinned twice by independent owners: struts.i18n.encoding in struts.xml for the Struts side, CharacterEncodingFilter for requests that continue down the chain, and additionally contentType/pageEncoding UTF-8 in every JSP.

ContextLoaderListener loads classpath:applicationContext.xml during web-app startup, so the datasource, seed script, SessionFactory and component-scanned service beans exist before the first request; no request-scoped Spring filter or listener such as an open-session-in-view filter is registered, so nothing in the request path manages a Hibernate session on an action's behalf.

src/struts.xml declares no <action>, <include>, <global-results> or <result-types> element: it sets struts.i18n.encoding and struts.objectFactory=spring, defines package basicstruts extending struts-default with the three project interceptors, defines stack auth-dafault as those three followed by defaultStack, and installs it via default-interceptor-ref so every convention-mapped endpoint runs it.

The stack name auth-dafault is spelled identically in the <interceptor-stack> declaration and the <default-interceptor-ref> reference, and that unconventional spelling is the only link between them: changing one side without the other silently disables all three project interceptors for every endpoint.

Convention mapping is the only routing table: @Namespace("/") and @ParentPackage("basicstruts") are declared once on Action4Result, the superclass of all eight action classes, and each @Action value is the entire URL below the context path, so renaming an @Action value changes the public URL with no XML edit.

All 36 result names are declared in a single @Results block on Action4Result (26 dispatcher forwards and 10 type="redirect" redirects), so no concrete action class declares @Result, @Results, @Namespace or @ParentPackage and subclasses only return a name.

struts.objectFactory=spring makes Struts obtain action and interceptor instances from the Spring root context, which is how their @Autowired service fields resolve; the concrete action classes carry no Spring stereotype, and the only @Component in the action package is on the shared superclass Action4Service.

AuthInterceptor gates only URIs starting with /fore, testing the suffix after the last "/fore" against a hard-coded whitelist of eight names (home, checkLogin, register, loginAjax, login, product, category, search); a non-whitelisted /fore URI without a session user gets response.sendRedirect("login.jsp") and a null return, so the remaining interceptors, parameter binding, the action body and any result never run.

No admin endpoint is protected: the 23 admin_* URLs never start with /fore so AuthInterceptor passes them straight through, and no other gate exists — web.xml declares no security-constraint and the admin JSP fragments add no check.

CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor overwrites session key "cs" with categoryService.list() on every /fore request before the action runs, and the two search fragments render that session list (5th-8th item in include/search.jsp, 8th-11th in include/simpleSearch.jsp); admin_* requests skip the query entirely.

CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor writes session key "cartTotalItemNumber" on every /fore request: with a session user it sums the number column over that user's order items whose order is null, otherwise it writes 0, and top.jsp renders it; because the write precedes the action invocation, a page produced by a cart-mutating action shows the pre-action count.

Request parameters bind through OGNL to public setters on the Action4* chain rather than to method arguments: dotted names instantiate nested objects and reach their setters (category.id yields a Category carrying only the id, page.start a Page built by its default constructor with count = 5, and the admin product forms post product.remark two levels down and product.category.id three levels down from the action), a repeated name binds an array (oiids), and multipart fields arrive as File img plus imgFileName/imgContentType.

Pagination is a binding convention: the admin pagination fragment emits relative ?page.start=... links, the list actions create a default Page when none is bound and set page.param to "&category.id=<id>" so those links keep the parent id, and Page.start plus the derived count drive the row window.

The default result type forwards to a JSP under web/ while keeping the action URL in the browser and the action on the value stack, whereas a type="redirect" result issues a fresh client request whose location may contain OGNL evaluated against the action (listPropertyPage, listProductPage, alipayPage); after a redirect only session state survives, which is why redirect-returning actions such as admin_property_delete call t2p() to populate the association their location dereferences, while admin_category_delete skips t2p() because /admin_category_list is a location with no OGNL in it.

Forwarded JSPs read session attributes (user in include/top.jsp, cs in the search fragments, cartTotalItemNumber in top.jsp, orderItems written by ForeAction#buy) and also read action properties such as ${categories}, ${products} and ${page.param}, even though no code under src/ or web/ calls setAttribute.

Requests whose path matches no @Action name invoke nothing from the stack: direct JSP hits (login.jsp and register.jsp linked from include/top.jsp, /registerSuccess.jsp reached by the registerSuccessPage redirect, /index.jsp) render without interceptors or bound data, the web/admin/*.jsp pages sit outside WEB-INF and are directly requestable so they render an empty table, and the relative img/ css/ js/ URLs are served from web/ by the container.

The root path / is not handled by a welcome file: web.xml declares no welcome-file-list and the launcher installs an exact-match rewrite of / to /forehome, while web/index.jsp redirects to "/forehome" when requested by name; the same /* filter mapping is why the H2 console runs on its own port 8082.

The three project interceptors do not compare the same URI: CategoryNamesBelowSearchInterceptor and CartTotalItemNumberInterceptor strip servletContext.getContextPath() before testing "/fore", while AuthInterceptor compares request.getRequestURI() directly; the launcher pins CONTEXT_PATH="/" where getContextPath() is empty, so under a non-root context path the auth gate would silently stop matching while the other two keep working.

No server-side validation exists on the write endpoints: no class in the Action4* chain extends ActionSupport (the chain ends at Object) and the single shared @Results block declares no input result, so malformed or empty parameters reach the action body and are saved as bound; the only checks in the repository are browser-side submit handlers on the two product forms, which test name/subTitle/originalPrice/promotePrice/stock and do not test the remark input those forms carry.

The remark column of the admin product table reads ${p.remark} off the JSTL loop variable declared by <c:forEach items="${products}" var="p">, i.e. a property of the iterated Product element rather than an action property, so a new column backed by an already-listed entity needs no new field on the Action4* chain while ${products} itself is still resolved from the value stack.
